name: ip-name-constraint-non-contiguous-mask-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees iPAddress contains an IPv4 constraint whose mask is non-contiguous: address 192.0.2.0 with mask 0xff00ff00 (255.0.255.0). RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 requires the mask to be contiguous — a run of 1-bits followed by a run of 0-bits — so this constraint is malformed and a conforming validator MUST reject the chain on the critical extension. Validators that mask byte-by-byte without checking contiguity will silently accept whichever leaf SAN happens to match address bits in the unmasked positions (here the first and third octets), producing surprising and unintended matches.
notes: Wire payload: NC SEQUENCE { permittedSubtrees [0] { GeneralSubtree { iPAddress [7 PRIMITIVE] address||mask } } } where address||mask is c0000200 ff00ff00. The leaf SAN 192.42.2.123 is *not* inside any sensible interpretation of the 192.0.2.0 subnet, but it shares the 0xff00ff00-masked bits (192.X.2.X) with the constraint address. A buggy mask-AND-and-compare implementation will accept it.
Constructed via unknown_extensions because cryptography.x509.NameConstraints normalises mask bytes to a contiguous CIDR prefix.
